# Part 0: Setup

```{r packages, message=F}
## Packages
### For plotting and data manipulation
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(patchwork)
library(maps)
library(ggmap)
### For PCA
library(corrplot)
library(factoextra)
### For CFA
library(psych)
library(lavaan) 
library(semPlot)
```

### Data Preparation

```{r wisconsin_data, message=F}
## Read in data
wdat <- read.csv('wisconsin_climate_data.csv') |> 
  rename(SoilClay_b0 = Soil_Clay_b0,
         SoilClay_b10 = Soil_Clay_b10,
         SoilClay_b30 = Soil_Clay_b30,
         SoilClay_b60 = Soil_Clay_b60,
         SoilClay_b100 = Soil_Clay_b100,
         SoilClay_b200 = Soil_Clay_b200,
         SoilWaterCap_b0 = Soil_Water_Cap_b0,
         SoilWaterCap_b10 = Soil_Water_Cap_b10,
         SoilWaterCap_b30 = Soil_Water_Cap_b30,
         SoilWaterCap_b60 = Soil_Water_Cap_b60,
         SoilWaterCap_b100 = Soil_Water_Cap_b100,
         SoilWaterCap_b200 = Soil_Water_Cap_b200)

## Get the Google Map for Wisconsin
wi_map <- get_map(c(-89.768969,44.773201), maptype = "satellite", zoom = 7)

## Get the outline of Wisconsin for Plots
wi_shape <- map_data("state") |> filter(region == "wisconsin")
```


```{r}
## Select Baseline Environment Variables for PCA
env_vars <- wdat |> select(
  ## Static Location Details
  Elevation, 
  Slope, 
  Aspect,
  ## Static Environment Features
  SoilClay_b10,
  SoilWaterCap_b10,
  ## MaxTemp  
  MaxTemp_mean,  ## (Baseline summer heat/pressure)
  MaxTemp_sd,    ## Max Temp Volatility
  ## MinTemp
  MinTemp_min,   ## Absolute Worst Winter Freeze,
  MinTemp_sd,    ## Min Temp Volatility,
  ## Precipitation
  Precip_mean,   ## Baseline Precip
  SWE_max,       ## Max Snowtotals
  ## Solar Radiation
  SurfaceRad_mean,
  ## VaporPressure
  VaporPressure_mean)

kable(colnames(env_vars), col.names=NULL,
      caption = "Baseline Environmental Variables") |> 
  kable_styling(font_size = 22)


## Select Stress Variables for CFA
stress_vars <- wdat |> select(
  NDVI_mean,
  NDWI_mean, 
  GPP_mean,
  Percent_NonVegetated,
  LST_mean,
  LST_sd
) |> scale()

kable(colnames(stress_vars), col.names=NULL,
      caption = "Variables for Evaluating Ecological Stress") |> 
  kable_styling(font_size = 22)

```

# Part 1: PCA for Baseline Environmental Variables

```{r}
# PCA ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## Correlation Matrix of env_vars
cor_mat <- cor(env_vars)
corrplot(cor_mat, 
         method = "color", 
         col = rev(COL2('RdBu', 200)),
         order = "hclust", 
         hclust.method = "ward.D2",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         tl.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.55,       # Shrinks the coefficient numbers
         tl.cex = 0.9,           # Shrinks the text labels (Variable names)
         cl.cex = 0.9,           # Shrinks the color legend text
         addgrid.col = "grey90",
         mar = c(0,0,2,0),
         title = "Environmental Variable Correlations")
```


```{r}
## PCA (scaled and Centered)  
pca_res <- prcomp(env_vars, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

## Explained Variance
var_exp <- summary(pca_res)$importance

## Scree Plot of Variance Decomposition
scree_plot <- fviz_eig(pca_res, 
                       addlabels = TRUE, 
                       ylim = c(0, 80),
                       barfill = "#3b5fc0", barcolor = "#3b5fc0", 
                       linecolor = "#c0392b", 
                       ggtheme = theme_bw(base_size=12)) +
  labs(title = "% Variance per PC",
       y='% of Var Explained')

##  Cumulative Variance Explained
cvar_df <- tibble(
  PC = (1:ncol(env_vars))[1:10],
  cvar = (var_exp[3,] * 100)[1:10]
)
cvar_plot <- ggplot(cvar_df, aes(PC, cvar)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3b5fc0") +
  geom_line(color = "#c0392b", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#c0392b", size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 75, linetype="dashed", color="grey40", lwd=1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,105), labels=function(x) paste0(x,"%")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:nrow(cvar_df)) +
  labs(title="Cumulative Variance Explained", x="PC", y="Cumulative %") +
  theme_bw(base_size=12)

scree_plot + cvar_plot

## Extract the First three PCs and add them to our data frame 
wdat$PC1 <- pca_res$x[,1]
wdat$PC2 <- pca_res$x[,2]
wdat$PC3 <- pca_res$x[,3]

```


```{r}
## Biplot of the first two PCs
biplot <- fviz_pca_biplot(pca_res,
                repel         = TRUE,
                col.var       = "#c0392b",
                labelsize = 6,
                col.ind       = "#3b5fc0",
                alpha.ind     = 0.25,
                label         = "var",
                ggtheme       = theme_bw(base_size = 12),
                title         = " Biplot") +
  labs(caption = "Arrows: variable loadings. Points: site scores.")
biplot
```


```{r}
## Look at the loadings for the first two PCs
cont <- pca_res$rotation^2
cont_df <- as_tibble(cont)
cont_df$Variable <- rownames(cont)

### Plot the contributions to PC1
plot_pc1_contrib <- ggplot(cont_df, aes(x = reorder(Variable, PC1), y = PC1)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#3b5fc0", color = "black") +
  coord_flip() + 
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Variable Contributions to PC1",
    x = "Environmental Variable",
    y = "Contribution to PC1 (%)"
  )

### Plot the contributions to PC2
plot_pc2_contrib <- ggplot(cont_df, aes(x = reorder(Variable, PC2), y = PC2)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#3b5fc0", color = "black") +
  coord_flip() + 
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Variable Contributions to PC2",
    x = "Environmental Variable",
    y = "Contribution to PC2 (%)"
  )

plot_pc1_contrib + plot_pc2_contrib

## Joint Contribution Plots
cont_df <- cont_df |> 
  select(Variable, PC1, PC2, PC3) |> 
  arrange(-PC1) 

loadings_long <- cont_df |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("PC"),
               names_to = "PC",
               values_to = "Loading") |> 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, rev(cont_df$Variable)))

joint_cont_plots <- ggplot(loadings_long, 
                           aes(x = Variable, y = Loading, fill = PC)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ PC, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Variable", y = "Loading", title = "PCA Loadings by Component") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

joint_cont_plots
```

# Part 2: Factor Analysis for Stress Variables

### EFA

```{r}
# EFA ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## Correlation Matrix of stress_vars
cor_mat <- cor(stress_vars)
corrplot(cor_mat, 
         method = "color", 
         col = rev(COL2('RdBu', 200)),
         order = "hclust", 
         hclust.method = "ward.D2",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         tl.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.6,       # Shrinks the coefficient numbers
         tl.cex = 0.9,           # Shrinks the text labels (Variable names)
         cl.cex = 0.9,           # Shrinks the color legend text
         addgrid.col = "grey90",
         mar = c(0,0,2,0),
         title = "Environmental Variable Correlations")
```

```{r}
## KMO test for if factor analysis is reasonable
kmo_res <- KMO(stress_vars)
kmo_res
```


```{r}
## EFA on a sample of the data
set.seed(52)
stress_samp <- stress_vars[sample(1:nrow(stress_vars), 400),]
parallel_test <- fa.parallel(stress_samp, 
                             fa = "fa",         
                             fm = "ml",         
                             main = "Scree Plot with Parallel Analysis",
                             plot=F)

## Fit the best factor structure
efa_result <- fa(stress_samp, 
                 nfactors = 2,       # Swap this with whatever Step 1 suggests
                 rotate = "oblimin", # Crucial: Allows the factors to be correlated
                 fm = "ml")          # Maximum Likelihood method

print(efa_result$loadings, cutoff = 0.3)


fa.diagram(efa_result, main = "EFA Factor Structure (Promax)", 
           cut=0.375, simple=FALSE)
```

### CFA

```{r message=F}
## Run CFA (data already scaled)
cfa_model <- '
  Biomass =~ NDVI_mean + NDWI_mean + Percent_NonVegetated + GPP_mean
  Metabolism =~ GPP_mean + LST_mean + LST_sd + NDWI_mean
  
'
fit <- cfa(cfa_model, data = stress_vars, std.lv = TRUE)
summary(fit, fit.measures=T)

## Plot the path diagram
custom_labels <- c(
  "NDVI",
  "Non-Veg",
  "NDWI",
  "GPP",
  "LST_mean",
  "LST_sd",
  "Biomass",
  "Metabolism"
)
semPaths(fit, 
         what='par',
         whatLabels = "std", 
         layout = "tree", 
         rotation = 2,
         edge.label.cex = 1.2, 
         color = list(man = "lightyellow", lat = "lightblue"),
         sizeMan = 8, sizeLat = 10,
         nodeLabels = custom_labels,
         title = FALSE)

## Get the loadings
standardizedSolution(fit) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(op == "=~") 

```


```{r}
## Extract the latent scores for each spatial point
latent_scores <- lavPredict(fit)
wdat$Biomass <- latent_scores[, "Biomass"]
wdat$Metabolism <- latent_scores[, "Metabolism"]

```

# Part 3: Clustering to identify modes of vulnerability

```{r}
## Select only the variables we want to cluster based on
cluster_data <- wdat |> select(PC1, PC2, PC3, Biomass, Metabolism)

## Rescale so that PCA and CFA are similarly weighted
cluster_data_scaled <-  scale(cluster_data)

# Use your scaled data!
fviz_nbclust(cluster_data_scaled, kmeans, method = "wss") 

```

### Using 4 Clusters
```{r}
## K-means with K=4
set.seed(12)
km_final <- kmeans(cluster_data_scaled, centers = 4, nstart = 10)
wdat$Cluster <- as.factor(km_final$cluster)
wdat$Cluster <- factor(wdat$Cluster, 
                       levels = c(3, 1, 4, 2), # The current order
                       labels = c("1", "2", "3", "4")) # The new numbers you are assigning

## Plot the Clusters
plot_clusters <- ggplot() +
  ## Draw the outline of Wisconsin
  geom_polygon(data = wi_shape, 
               aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group), 
               fill = "gray95", 
               alpha=1, 
               color = "black", 
               linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = wdat, 
             aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude, col=Cluster), 
             size = 1.5, 
             alpha = 0.8) +
  ## Keep the map proportional
  labs(title = "Clustered Locations")

plot_clusters_map <- ggmap(wi_map)+
  ## Draw the outline of Wisconsin
  geom_polygon(data = wi_shape, 
               aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group), 
               fill = "gray95", 
               alpha=0, 
               color = "black", 
               linewidth = 0.5) +
  ## Add our sampled locations
  geom_point(data = wdat, 
             aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude, col=Cluster), 
             size = 1.5, 
             alpha = 0.8) +
  ## Keep the map proportional
  labs(title = "(a) Clustered Locations")

plot_clusters + plot_clusters_map

## Calculate means for each cluster
cluster_summary <- wdat |>
  group_by(Cluster) |>
  summarize(
    N = n(),
    Mean_Biomass = mean(Biomass),
    Mean_Metabolism = mean(Metabolism),
    Mean_PC1 = mean(PC1),
    Mean_PC2 = mean(PC2),
    Mean_PC3 = mean(PC3)
  )

kable(cluster_summary)

## Plot the cluster summaries
cplot <- ggplot(wdat, aes(y = Biomass, x = Metabolism, color = factor(Cluster))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_label(data = cluster_summary, 
             aes(y = Mean_Biomass, x = Mean_Metabolism, label = paste("Cluster", Cluster)),
             color = "black", fontface = "bold", size=2, alpha=0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "(b) Metabolism vs Biomass",
       y = "Biomass", 
       x = "Metabolism ",
       color = "Cluster") + theme(legend.position = "none")

cplot_PCA <- ggplot(wdat, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = factor(Cluster))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_label(data = cluster_summary, 
             aes(x = Mean_PC1, y = Mean_PC2, label = paste("Cluster", Cluster)),
             color = "black", fontface = "bold", size=2, alpha=0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "(c) PC1 vs PC2",
       x = "PC1", 
       y = "PC2 ",
       color = "Cluster") + theme(legend.position = "none")

## Show plots
joint_plot <- 
  plot_clusters_map + 
  (cplot / cplot_PCA) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(0.4, 0.6))
joint_plot
```
